skill.summary: Build API test plans and sample requests for REST, GraphQL, authentication, validation, and performance checks.

security_audit.summary: All 119 static findings were adjudicated as false positives caused by Markdown code fences, JavaScript template literals, placeholder API URLs, and normal API testing examples. The reviewed file contains documentation and sample commands only; no prompt injection, covert exfiltration, or automatic execution path was found. Minor documentation hardening is recommended for credential and load testing examples.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer header-based API key examples and label query-parameter keys as legacy or discouraged because URLs can be logged.
Remind users to keep real tokens in environment variables or secret managers instead of prompts, files, or examples.
Add a clear note to run load tests only against APIs the user owns or has written permission to test.

content.user_title: Test APIs With Request and Validation Guidance
content.value_statement: API testing often misses authentication, schema, and error cases. This skill helps create endpoint checks, sample requests, collections, and performance tests.
actual_capabilities: Creates curl examples for GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, and GraphQL requests.
Drafts JavaScript and Python request examples using fetch, axios, and requests.
Builds API test cases for status codes, schemas, authentication, and error paths.
Outlines Postman collection structures with variables and test scripts.
Provides load testing examples using Apache Bench and Artillery.
Lists common HTTP status codes and API testing best practices.
limitations: Does not execute requests unless the hosting agent runs the generated commands or scripts.
Uses placeholder domains and credentials that must be replaced before use.
Does not verify live API behavior without an accessible endpoint and authorization.
Load testing examples require permission from the API owner.

use_cases.title: Endpoint Smoke Tests
use_cases.description: Create quick request checks for new REST endpoints before merging changes.

use_cases.title: Contract Validation
use_cases.description: Draft schema, status code, and error-path tests for regression coverage.

use_cases.title: Performance Baseline
use_cases.description: Plan controlled load tests for staging APIs with concurrency and reporting examples.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Endpoint Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use api-tester to create GET and POST tests for /api/users. Include headers, sample bodies, and expected status codes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Authentication Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use api-tester for my protected API. Generate tests for valid tokens, missing tokens, invalid tokens, and role-based access.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Postman Collection Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use api-tester to outline a Postman collection for these endpoints: [list endpoints]. Include variables, test assertions, and error cases.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Full API Test Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use api-tester to design REST and GraphQL tests for [service]. Include contract validation, negative cases, rate limits, and staged load testing.

output_examples.input: Need quick tests for GET /api/users and POST /api/users.
output_examples.output: Returns a compact test plan with request methods, headers, sample fields, expected status codes, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: Prepare authentication tests for a protected endpoint.
output_examples.output: Produces cases for valid tokens, missing tokens, expired tokens, invalid roles, and expected 401 or 403 responses.

output_examples.input: Plan a staging load test for user search.
output_examples.output: Suggests concurrency levels, duration, success criteria, rate-limit checks, and a reporting outline.

best_practices: Use staging endpoints and test accounts before testing production APIs.
Keep real tokens in environment variables or secret managers, not in prompts or files.
Define expected status codes, schemas, and error messages before generating tests.
anti_patterns: Do not run load tests against third-party APIs without written authorization.
Do not paste real bearer tokens, passwords, or API keys into shared prompts.
Do not treat generated examples as proof that a live endpoint works.

faq.question: Does this skill call APIs by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides testing guidance and examples. Actual requests only run if the agent executes generated commands or scripts.

faq.question: Can it create Postman collections?
faq.answer: It can outline collection structure, variables, and assertions that you can adapt for Postman.

faq.question: Does it support GraphQL?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes query, variable, and mutation testing patterns for GraphQL APIs.

faq.question: Can it help with authentication testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers bearer tokens, API keys, basic auth, OAuth flows, and negative authorization cases.

faq.question: Is it safe for production load testing?
faq.answer: Use production only with explicit approval, limits, and monitoring. Staging is safer for initial load tests.

faq.question: What should I provide in a prompt?
faq.answer: Provide endpoint paths, methods, expected responses, authentication type, and schema or rate-limit requirements.
